subject: science
domain: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer
skillName: How We See Objects with Light

items.prompt:
We can see objects because light
A) is made by our eyes
B) reflects off them into our eyes
C) stays still
D) has color only
items.answer: B) reflects off them into our eyes

steps: Reflected light entering the eye lets us see.

items.prompt:
In a completely dark room with no light, you
A) see everything clearly
B) cannot see objects
C) see only red
D) see better

steps: No light means nothing reflects into your eyes.

items.prompt:
Our eyes see by
A) sending out rays
B) receiving light
C) making darkness
D) touching objects

steps: Eyes detect light that enters them.

items.prompt:
For you to see a ball, light must reflect off it and
A) enter your eye
B) leave the room
C) turn into sound
D) disappear

steps: Reflected light must reach the eye to be seen.

items.prompt:
A model of seeing connects three parts with arrows:
A) source, object, eye
B) eye, sound, color
C) heat, light, wire
D) water, wind, rock

steps: Light goes source to object to eye.

items.prompt:
A student says eyes work like flashlights. The correct idea is that eyes
A) shine light on objects
B) receive light that reflects off objects
C) make objects glow
D) create darkness
items.answer: B) receive light that reflects off objects

steps: Seeing happens when reflected light enters the eye.

items.prompt:
You see the Moon at night because
A) the Moon makes its own light
B) sunlight reflects off the Moon and enters your eye
C) your eyes glow
D) the Moon is close
items.answer: B) sunlight reflects off the Moon and enters your eye

steps: Sunlight reflects off the Moon to your eye.

items.prompt:
A shiny object looks brighter than a dull one in the same light because it
A) makes its own light
B) reflects more light into your eyes
C) is bigger
D) is closer
items.answer: B) reflects more light into your eyes

steps: More reflected light reaching the eye looks brighter.
